ran:

evidence: dorder_io_block.c:95 'if ((rangtab = memAlloc (...)) == NULL) {' after the header fprintf; :103-121 'if (intSave (stream, rangtab[...]) != 1) goto fail;' with unchecked 'putc' at :106, :110, :117, :121; :126 'fail:' :128 'memFree (rangtab);'
upstream_change: addcd163d9 'Bugfix: prevent memory leak and check (almost) all outputs [report R. Perry]'

upstream_fix_review.details: Allocation moved after the header write (no leak on 'bad output (1)'), every intSave checked with goto fail, single memFree on both paths, 0/1 return. Still unchecked ('almost'): the four putc() separators (:106, :110, :117, :121), whose failure is caught only if a later intSave fails, and the final stdio flush: no fflush/ferror, so a write error on the last buffered block (any small ordering) returns 0 (shown with /dev/full). Not in this routine: dorderSaveTree2 agrees on the result only under SCOTCH_DEBUG_DORDER1 (dorder_io_tree.c:160-169), so non-root processes return 0 while the root returns 1. The sequential writers (order_io.c) do not check putc either.
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Our 0006 guarded the two trailing writes with 'if (o == 1)' and freed on both returns; his goto-fail version is equivalent and also moves the allocation after the header write (better). Dropped.
